heroLead: Ossineke sits along Lake Huron south of Alpena, and the mineral history under this stretch of shoreline and farmland runs through limestone quarrying as much as it does oil and gas.
intro: Ossineke is a small unincorporated community in Alpena County along the Lake Huron shoreline, surrounded by a mix of farm land and forest. Like much of Alpena County, mineral ownership here can involve limestone or aggregate rights alongside, or instead of, oil and gas rights, since quarrying has such deep roots in this part of the state.

sections.heading: Checking what kind of mineral interest you actually hold
paragraphs: Before anything else, it's worth confirming whether your family's mineral interest near Ossineke covers oil and gas, limestone or aggregate, or both, since a deed here can address them separately depending on when and how the property changed hands. The Alpena County register of deeds is where that history is recorded.

sections.heading: What oil and gas activity near Ossineke looks like
paragraphs: Ossineke sits outside the Antrim Shale core, so any oil and gas history here ties more to Traverse Group and Devonian reef trends rather than the dense biogenic shale gas play further inland. Activity varies section by section, and we check your specific parcel and current statements before saying anything about value.

sections.heading: What we need to evaluate an Ossineke-area interest
paragraphs: Send your deed or probate document, any royalty statements or division orders you've received, and note whether your paperwork mentions limestone, aggregate, or oil and gas specifically. That distinction shapes how the interest gets evaluated from the start.
We'll check the recorded chain of title alongside current production before saying anything definite about value.

faqs.question: Is Ossineke part of the Antrim Shale play?
faqs.answer: No, this area sits outside the Antrim core. Any oil and gas history near Ossineke ties more to Traverse Group and Devonian reef formations in the Michigan Basin.

faqs.question: Could my mineral interest near Ossineke include limestone rights?
faqs.answer: It's possible. Alpena County has a long history of limestone quarrying, and some deeds address limestone or aggregate rights separately from oil and gas. Check your deed language or pull the recorded chain of title to confirm.

faqs.question: How do I find out if there's oil and gas production tied to my Ossineke-area interest?
faqs.answer: Check any royalty statements you've received for an operator name and division order, or contact the Alpena County register of deeds to check for recorded leases against your parcel.

faqs.question: Is a non-producing mineral interest near Ossineke worth anything?
faqs.answer: It can carry some speculative value tied to future leasing potential, but that's a different situation from a producing royalty interest with real income history behind it. We'll be upfront about which one applies.
